sections.h2: Selling in East Hampton: the main routes
sections.html:
East Hampton sellers can put the house on the market, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase. Cash helps most when a certificate of occupancy is unresolved, repairs were postponed, or a tenant is living there, since cash buyers often take a property as it stands.

Start with the permit file, any rental registry paperwork and your latest tax bills. If the house is rented, update the registry whenever the tenancy changes so the town's record matches who lives there. Then weigh a quick close against the higher price a full market sale might bring. A sale that depends on a new certificate should leave room in the schedule, because the Building Department has a backlog.

East Hampton is the easternmost town in New York, at the far end of Long Island's South Fork in Suffolk County. It covers 74.33 square miles and includes the village of East Hampton, part of the village of Sag Harbor, and hamlets such as Montauk, Amagansett, Wainscott, Springs, Northwest Harbor and Napeague. Water borders it on several sides, so a house in Montauk and a house in Springs reach very different buyers. Montauk is New York's largest fishing port, and summer crowds still drive much of the economy, which shapes who shops for a house there and when.

Population is 29,400. About 77.8 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, and the typical value of those homes is $1,178,500. Typical household income is $132,348 and typical monthly rent is $2,578. With values this high, many sales pass the $1 million line where the state adds a residential tax for buyers, so look at price and closing figures carefully with your attorney.

The Receiver of Taxes prepares more than 24,000 bills and distributes the money to Suffolk County, the town, nine fire and fire protection districts, six school districts with five libraries and one museum district, five lighting districts, five road and water connection districts, and special use districts.

Each collection season ends on June 1, and the online payment portal closes the next day. After that, payments with penalties and interest go to the Suffolk County Comptroller in Riverhead. The portal still lets you view and print bills and receipts. The town recommends certified mail with your tax map number if you pay late.

The Assessor's Office also keeps ownership records, handles state exemptions and maintains the street address database used for E-911 dispatch. New STAR applicants must register with the state tax department to receive a STAR check. Seller or buyer, mark March 1 on the calendar if an exemption is involved. A seller who thinks the tentative roll overstates the value should raise it during the grievance period that opens May 1, since the final roll on July 1 sets the figure used afterward.

sections.h2: Certificate of occupancy on a sale
sections.html:
The Town Code requires an updated certificate of occupancy on any change of ownership, with two exceptions. Under Chapter 102-14, no new certificate is needed if one was issued within six months before the transfer, or if the transfer only moves the property to a trust, LLC or similar entity for estate planning with the same beneficial owner.

The Town Board paused enforcement on March 10, 2026, and the pause runs retroactively from January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2026. The Building Department still processes applications, and it tells sellers to keep applying. Roughly six in ten applications involve improvements built without a permit, which lengthens review.

  • The updated certificate fee is $600.
  • Open building permits must be closed out, or renewal fees and violations can follow.
  • A closing in January 2027 or later falls after the stated end of the pause, so ask the department whether it will be extended.

Every Building Department application must be filed digitally through the town's OpenGov portal, and payments are made online, not at the counter. Counter drop-off runs 8:30 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays, with the first half hour reserved for contractors and 9:00 to 10:30 am for the general public.

A zoning amendment effective July 1, 2025 limits gross floor area for a single-family residence to 7 percent of lot area plus 1,500 square feet or 10,000 square feet, whichever is less. Any building permit that includes clearing needs a staked survey showing the clearing envelope. If the house is rented, the rental registry requires a signed, notarized update form every time the tenancy changes.

The Peconic Bay Community Preservation Fund is financed by a 2 percent real estate transfer tax, created by Town Law 64-e in 1998 and administered under Tax Law section 31-d. A 2024 State Comptroller audit reported $127.2 million deposited during 2021 and 2022 and 2,352 acres of open space, farmland, parks and historic sites preserved through the end of 2022.

Ask your closing attorney whether the tax applies to your sale, which side pays it, and whether an exemption fits. The state also charges $2 per $500 of price through the TP-584 return, plus an extra 1 percent on residences at $1 million or more.

A tenant in place complicates a sale in two ways. First, the town's rental registry needs a signed, notarized update form every time the tenancy changes, and a sale that ends a tenancy is a change. Second, a buyer will want to know whether the rental was ever permitted. Open building permits tied to the rental must be closed out, or renewal fees and violations can follow.

Pull the registry record and the permit history together before an offer arrives. A cash buyer will often take a tenant-occupied house as it stands, but the price will reflect the open questions, so the cleaner your file, the stronger your number.

Gather the certificate of occupancy status, the rental registry form if you have a tenant, and the latest tax bills before you talk to any buyer. Then request offers and compare them with what you owe. A cash sale cuts out financing delays and showings. It does not cut out the certificate question, the Community Preservation Fund tax, or the transfer tax return, so ask your attorney who handles each one.

Closing day brings payoffs from your proceeds, delivery of the deed, and the state filings that follow.

faqs.q: Is East Hampton a town or a village?
faqs.a: Both exist. The Town of East Hampton is the large municipality of 74.33 square miles, and the incorporated village of East Hampton sits inside it, along with part of Sag Harbor and several hamlets.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in East Hampton?
faqs.a: Roughly $1,178,500 for homes occupied by their owners. Household income in the middle of the range is $132,348.

faqs.q: Do I need an updated certificate of occupancy to sell in East Hampton?
faqs.a: The code requires one when ownership changes, though enforcement is paused through December 31, 2026. The Building Department still takes applications, charges $600, and advises sellers to apply.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in East Hampton?
faqs.a: The third Tuesday in May. The tentative roll is posted May 1, and the final roll arrives July 1.

faqs.q: Who do I pay if I missed the East Hampton tax deadline?
faqs.a: After June 1 the Town no longer accepts payment. Late payments, with penalties and interest, go to the Suffolk County Comptroller.
